signature.name: Kasubi Tombs
signature.detail: A UNESCO World Heritage site and the royal burial ground of the Buganda kings, this thatched-domed complex is the most important cultural site in Uganda. It is a must-see for understanding Buganda history and traditions. Practical tip: visit in the morning to avoid crowds; entry is by guided tour, and modest dress is appreciated.

signature.name: Gaddafi National Mosque
signature.detail: One of Africa's largest mosques, it offers a striking blend of Islamic architecture and panoramic views from its minaret. The climb to the top is worth it for a 360-degree look over Kampala. Practical tip: dress conservatively (women should cover hair and shoulders), and avoid prayer times; a small entry fee applies.

signature.name: Namugongo Martyrs Shrine
signature.detail: A major pilgrimage site commemorating the 22 Ugandan martyrs, with a moving history and impressive modern basilica. It is especially vibrant during the June 3 pilgrimage. Practical tip: go on a weekday for a quieter visit; the site is about 12 km northeast of the centre and reachable by taxi.

signature.name: Baha'i House of Worship
signature.detail: The only Baha'i temple in Africa, set in peaceful gardens on a hill with views over the city. Its distinctive nine-sided dome and tranquil atmosphere make it a refreshing stop. Practical tip: open daily, free entry, and easy to combine with a visit to the nearby Uganda National Museum.
